<script src="libs/d3.min.js"></script>

```{julia}
#| output: false
using RDF, Graphs, DataFrames, Statistics, Dates
import JSON
include("graphtools.jl")

const DS = rdf_read(joinpath("..", "julia_ecosystem.nq"))
const G  = DS.default_graph

snapmetric(pred) = snapmetric_ds(DS, pred)

n_pkg    = scalar(DS, "SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?p) AS ?n) WHERE { ?p a jl:Package }")
# distinct accounts that appear as a contributor (not just any foaf:nick holder,
# which would also count repo owners who never committed)
n_people = scalar(DS, "SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?person) AS ?n) WHERE { ?pkg dcterms:contributor ?person }")
n_dep    = scalar(DS, "SELECT (COUNT(*) AS ?n) WHERE { ?a jl:dependsOn ?b }")
n_jll    = scalar(DS, "SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?p) AS ?n) WHERE { ?p jl:isJLL true }")

# Read the snapshot date straight from the graph so prose never drifts from data.
SNAP_DATE  = string(scalar(DS, "SELECT ?d WHERE { GRAPH ?g { ?s a jl:Snapshot ; jl:observedAt ?d } } LIMIT 1"))
SNAP_HUMAN = Dates.format(Date(SNAP_DATE), dateformat"d U yyyy")

# Standard-library coverage: how many of this Julia's stdlibs are registered in
# General (and therefore graph nodes) versus not. Computed, not hardcoded.
allpkgnames  = String.(q(DS, "SELECT ?name WHERE { ?p a jl:Package ; rdfs:label ?name }").name)
n_stdlib     = length(STDLIBS)
n_stdlib_reg = count(isstdlib, allpkgnames)

TS  = trust_surface(DS)
NET = network_data(DS)
IDX = package_index(DS, TS)
nothing
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
All figures are computed from a single dataset describing the General registry
on **`{julia} SNAP_HUMAN`**: every registered package, its dependency edges,
its GitHub repository metadata, and its commit authors. Construction and known
limitations are described in [Methods & limitations](#methods).
:::

# Explore it yourself {#explore}

The whole graph is queryable, live, in your browser — open the
[**SPARQL explorer**](https://mthelm85.github.io/JuliaEcosystemGraph/explorer.html)
to ask your own questions of it at any point. The rest of this page walks
through some of what it can show.

# Registry totals

```{julia}
#| output: asis
stat(v, k) = """<div style="flex:1;min-width:140px;text-align:center">
  <div style="font-size:2.4rem;font-weight:700;line-height:1">$(fmt_int(v))</div>
  <div style="color:#888">$k</div></div>"""
println("""<div style="display:flex;gap:2rem;flex-wrap:wrap;margin:1.4rem 0">
$(stat(n_pkg,"packages"))$(stat(n_people,"contributors"))$(stat(n_dep,"dependency links"))$(stat(n_jll,"binary wrappers"))
</div>""")
```

`_jll` wrappers account for `{julia} round(Int, 100*n_jll/n_pkg)`% of the
registry (`{julia} fmt_int(n_jll)` packages). Being BinaryBuilder-generated
rather than hand-authored, they are excluded from the ranked analyses below,
as are standard libraries — the registry represents standard libraries only
partially (see [Methods](#methods)), so including them would be inconsistent.
"Contributors" counts distinct GitHub accounts credited with at least one
commit to at least one registered package. Exclusions are stated per figure.

# Dependency load: direct and transitive dependents {#load-bearing}

For each package, the direct-dependent count is its in-degree in the
dependency graph; the transitive-dependent count is the number of packages
from which it is reachable. The table ranks by the latter, over registered
packages excluding standard libraries and JLL wrappers (see note).

```{julia}
#| output: asis
ld = q(DS, """
  SELECT ?name ?dir ?trans WHERE {
    GRAPH ?g { ?s jl:forPackage ?pkg ; jl:directDependents ?dir ; jl:transitiveDependents ?trans . }
    ?pkg rdfs:label ?name .
    FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?pkg jl:isJLL true }
  }""")
ld.name = String.(ld.name); ld.dir = Int.(ld.dir); ld.trans = Int.(ld.trans)
filter!(r -> !isstdlib(r.name), ld)
sort!(ld, :trans, rev=true)
lines = ["| # | Package | Direct | Transitive |", "|--:|:--|--:|--:|"]
for (i, r) in enumerate(eachrow(first(ld, 15)))
    push!(lines, "| $i | $(juliahub_link(r.name)) | $(fmt_int(r.dir)) | **$(fmt_int(r.trans))** |")
end
println(join(lines, "\n"))
```

: Registered packages (excluding standard libraries and JLL wrappers) ranked
by transitive dependents. {.striped tbl-colwidths="[6,44,22,28]"}

Direct and transitive counts differ by one to two orders of magnitude at the
top of the distribution. The highest-ranked package, `{julia} ld.name[1]`, has
`{julia} fmt_int(ld.dir[1])` direct dependents but is reachable from
**`{julia} fmt_int(ld.trans[1])`** packages
(`{julia} round(Int, 100*ld.trans[1]/n_pkg)`% of the registry). The ranking is
dominated by low-level infrastructure — array and iterator interfaces, compiler
and macro utilities, serialization, and numerical primitives — rather than
end-user libraries.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal"}
Source: registry dependency graph (latest registered version). Direct = number
of packages declaring this one as a direct dependency; transitive = number of
packages from which it is reachable, computed on the whole graph with
strongly-connected-component condensation (cycle-safe). Standard libraries are
excluded here because the registry represents them incompletely: only
`{julia} n_stdlib_reg` of Julia's `{julia} n_stdlib` standard libraries are
registered in General (e.g. `TOML`, `Artifacts`) and would otherwise rank near
the top, while the rest (`LinearAlgebra`, `Random`, …) are not registry entries
and are absent from the graph entirely. See [Methods](#methods).
:::

# GitHub stars versus dependency PageRank {#invisible}

GitHub stars and dependency PageRank measure different things: stars are a
user-facing popularity signal, PageRank is computed over the dependency graph
and weights a package by the importance of the packages that depend on it. The
scatter below plots the two on log axes.

```{julia}
#| output: asis
sc = q(DS, """
  SELECT ?name ?stars ?pr ?dep WHERE {
    GRAPH ?g { ?s jl:forPackage ?pkg ; jl:stars ?stars ; jl:pagerank ?pr ; jl:directDependents ?dep . }
    ?pkg rdfs:label ?name .
    FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?pkg jl:isJLL true }
  }""")
recs = [Dict("name"=>String(r.name), "stars"=>Int(r.stars),
             "pr"=>Float64(r.pr), "dep"=>Int(r.dep))
        for r in eachrow(sc) if !isstdlib(String(r.name))]
embed_json("scatter", recs)
```

::: {.column-page}
<div id="scatter-viz" style="position:relative"></div>
:::

<script>
window.__viz = window.__viz || {};
window.__viz.scatter = function () {
  const data = window.__DATA_scatter.filter(d => d.stars > 0 && d.pr > 0);
  const W = 900, H = 560, m = {t:20,r:20,b:55,l:70};
  const root = d3.select("#scatter-viz");
  root.selectAll("*").remove();
  const svg = root.append("svg").attr("viewBox", [0,0,W,H])
    .attr("style","max-width:100%;height:auto;font:11px system-ui");
  const x = d3.scaleLog().domain([1, d3.max(data,d=>d.stars)*1.1]).range([m.l, W-m.r]);
  const y = d3.scaleLog().domain([d3.min(data,d=>d.pr)*0.9, d3.max(data,d=>d.pr)*1.1]).range([H-m.b, m.t]);
  svg.append("g").attr("transform",`translate(0,${H-m.b})`).call(d3.axisBottom(x).ticks(6,"~s"));
  svg.append("g").attr("transform",`translate(${m.l},0)`).call(d3.axisLeft(y).ticks(6,"~e"));
  svg.append("text").attr("x",(W)/2).attr("y",H-12).attr("text-anchor","middle").attr("fill","#555").text("GitHub stars →");
  svg.append("text").attr("transform","rotate(-90)").attr("x",-(H)/2).attr("y",16).attr("text-anchor","middle").attr("fill","#555").text("↑ dependency PageRank");

  const tip = root.append("div").attr("style",
    "position:absolute;pointer-events:none;background:#222;color:#fff;padding:4px 8px;border-radius:4px;font:11px system-ui;opacity:0;transition:opacity .1s;z-index:10");

  svg.append("g").selectAll("circle").data(data).join("circle")
    .attr("cx",d=>x(d.stars)).attr("cy",d=>y(d.pr)).attr("r",3)
    .attr("fill","#4c78a8").attr("fill-opacity",0.35)
    .on("mousemove",(e,d)=>{
      tip.style("opacity",1)
        .style("left",(e.offsetX+12)+"px").style("top",(e.offsetY-10)+"px")
        .html(`<b>${d.name}</b><br>${d.stars.toLocaleString()} stars · ${d.dep} dependents`);
    })
    .on("mouseleave",()=>tip.style("opacity",0));

  // Label high-PageRank / low-star points. Place highest-PageRank first and
  // greedily skip any label whose box would overlap one already placed, so the
  // shown labels stay legible; unlabeled points still name themselves on hover.
  const cand = data.filter(d => d.pr > 0.004 && d.stars < 400).sort((a,b)=>b.pr-a.pr);
  const boxes = [], chosen = [];
  for (const d of cand) {
    const lx = x(d.stars)+5, ly = y(d.pr)-4, w = d.name.length*5.4, h = 11;
    const b = {x1:lx, y1:ly-h, x2:lx+w, y2:ly};
    if (boxes.some(p => !(b.x2 < p.x1 || b.x1 > p.x2 || b.y2 < p.y1 || b.y1 > p.y2))) continue;
    boxes.push(b); chosen.push({d, lx, ly});
  }
  svg.append("g").selectAll("text").data(chosen).join("text")
    .attr("x",c=>c.lx).attr("y",c=>c.ly).attr("fill","#c0392b").attr("font-size",10)
    .attr("paint-order","stroke").attr("stroke","white").attr("stroke-width",2.5)
    .text(c=>c.d.name);
};
</script>

The two quantities are weakly correlated. The points labeled in red are those
with high PageRank but fewer than 400 stars — high dependency load paired with
limited direct attention. These are typically low-level dependencies that are
rarely installed directly and so accumulate few stars relative to their
position in the graph.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal"}
Source: registry dependency graph (PageRank) × GitHub stars. Stars are a
repository-level metric and accumulate over a package's lifetime, so older
packages are advantaged. PageRank is one of several centrality measures; the
raw dependent counts in the table above are an alternative.
:::

# High transitive-to-direct dependent ratios {#hidden}

The ratio of transitive to direct dependents identifies packages with a small
number of direct dependents but a large transitive footprint — utilities
depended upon by a few foundational packages that are themselves widely
depended upon. These do not appear in star or direct-dependent rankings. The
table filters to packages with at least 1,000 transitive dependents and sorts
by the ratio.

```{julia}
#| output: asis
hid = q(DS, """
  SELECT ?name ?dir ?trans WHERE {
    GRAPH ?g { ?s jl:forPackage ?pkg ; jl:directDependents ?dir ; jl:transitiveDependents ?trans . }
    ?pkg rdfs:label ?name .
    FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?pkg jl:isJLL true }
  }""")
hid.name = String.(hid.name); hid.dir = Int.(hid.dir); hid.trans = Int.(hid.trans)
# floor the transitive reach so the ratio measures real infrastructure, not noise
filter!(r -> r.trans >= 1000 && r.dir >= 1 && !isstdlib(r.name), hid)
hid.ratio = hid.trans ./ hid.dir
sort!(hid, :ratio, rev=true)
lines = ["| Package | Direct | Transitive | Reach multiple |", "|:--|--:|--:|--:|"]
for r in eachrow(first(hid, 12))
    push!(lines, "| $(juliahub_link(r.name)) | $(fmt_int(r.dir)) | $(fmt_int(r.trans)) | $(fmt_int(r.ratio))× |")
end
println(join(lines, "\n"))
```

: Packages with few direct but many transitive dependents, ranked by ratio.
Restricted to ≥ 1,000 transitive dependents. {.striped tbl-colwidths="[40,15,20,25]"}

`DataValueInterfaces` is the extreme case: 2 direct dependents,
`{julia} fmt_int(first(hid.trans))` transitive. Such packages are not
identifiable from stars or direct-dependent counts; the ratio requires the
full transitive closure.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal"}
Source: registry dependency graph. "Reach multiple" is transitive ÷ direct
dependents. The 1,000-transitive floor removes packages whose high ratio comes
from a negligible footprint. JLL wrappers are excluded.
:::

# Contributor reach {#people}

Joining commit-author data across all repositories gives, per contributor, the
number of distinct packages they have committed to. The distribution is
long-tailed; the highest-reach accounts appear below.

```{julia}
#| output: asis
reach = q(DS, """
  SELECT ?login (COUNT(DISTINCT ?pkg) AS ?n) WHERE {
    ?pkg dcterms:contributor ?person . ?person foaf:nick ?login .
    FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?pkg jl:isJLL true }
  } GROUP BY ?login ORDER BY DESC(?n) LIMIT 20""")
reach.login = String.(reach.login); reach.n = Int.(reach.n)
lines = ["| # | Account | Packages contributed to |", "|--:|:--|--:|"]
for (i, r) in enumerate(eachrow(reach))
    push!(lines, "| $i | $(github_link(r.login)) | $(fmt_int(r.n)) |")
end
println(join(lines, "\n"))
```

: Accounts by number of distinct non-wrapper packages committed to. Automated
and AI-authored accounts are included (see note). {.striped tbl-colwidths="[8,52,40]"}

Reach measures the number of packages touched, not amount or significance of
work. A single automated or one-line commit counts the same as sustained
authorship, and the measure captures neither review, triage, documentation,
nor design. High reach frequently reflects release-engineering and
infrastructure roles (registry maintenance, the binary-build system, CI). A
GitHub account is not necessarily one person (handle renames, shared or
organizational accounts).

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal"}
Source: contributor lists from each package's GitHub repository, joined across
the ecosystem. Automated and AI-authored accounts are shown as recorded — for
example `claude` (Anthropic), which records commits authored by Claude Code.
High-volume CI bots (`JuliaTagBot`, `CompatHelper`, `dependabot`, and similar)
are filtered during data collection and are absent from the dataset entirely.
:::

# Inactivity among depended-upon packages {#fragile}

Cross-referencing repository activity against dependent counts identifies
packages that are archived or long inactive while retaining many dependents.
The aggregate below is over the 500 most depended-upon independent packages.

```{julia}
#| output: asis
pushed = Dict(String(r.name) => r.v for r in eachrow(snapmetric("lastPushedAt")))
arch   = Set(String(r.name) for r in eachrow(snapmetric("isArchived")) if r.v == true)
depmap = Dict(String(r.name) => Int(r.v) for r in eachrow(snapmetric("directDependents")))

const INACTIVE_YEARS = 4
cutoff = string(Date(SNAP_DATE) - Year(INACTIVE_YEARS))
stale(name) = name in arch || (haskey(pushed, name) && string(pushed[name]) < cutoff)

ranked = sort([(n, d) for (n, d) in depmap if !isstdlib(n) && !occursin("_jll", n)]; by=last, rev=true)
top500 = first(ranked, 500)
n_stale = count(x -> stale(x[1]), top500)
println("Of the **500 most depended-upon** independent packages, ",
        "**$n_stale** are archived or have no commit in the $INACTIVE_YEARS years ",
        "preceding the snapshot.\n")
```

```{julia}
#| output: asis
rows = [(n, d, get(pushed, n, missing), n in arch) for (n, d) in top500 if stale(n)]
sort!(rows, by = x -> x[2], rev = true)
lines = ["| Package | Dependents | Last commit | |", "|:--|--:|:--|:--|"]
for (n, d, p, a) in first(rows, 20)
    when = a ? "—" : string(p)[1:min(10, length(string(p)))]
    tag  = a ? "*archived*" : ""
    push!(lines, "| $(juliahub_link(n)) | $(fmt_int(d)) | $when | $tag |")
end
println(join(lines, "\n"))
```

: Inactive packages (archived, or no commit in four years) among the 500 most
depended-upon, ordered by dependent count. {.striped tbl-colwidths="[40,20,25,15]"}

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal"}
Source: GitHub push timestamps and archive flags × registry dependents. The
push timestamp is repository-level, so a subpackage in an active monorepo may
appear inactive or vice versa. Dependency edges are the latest registered
version only.
:::

# The dependency-graph k-core {#shape}

The k-core is the maximal subgraph in which every vertex has degree ≥ k, on the
undirected dependency graph with JLL wrappers and standard libraries removed.
`k` is set automatically to the smallest value whose k-core has at most a few
hundred nodes, so the layout stays legible; the resulting `k` and node count
are shown below the figure. Node size and color both encode PageRank. Hover for
a name; click a node to highlight its neighborhood — the packages it connects to
directly — and see its record below.

```{julia}
#| output: asis
prmax = isempty(NET.nodes) ? 0.0 : maximum(n["pr"] for n in NET.nodes)
embed_json("net", Dict("nodes"=>NET.nodes, "links"=>NET.links, "prmax"=>prmax, "k"=>NET.k))
```

::: {.column-page}
<div id="net-viz" style="position:relative"></div>
<div id="net-caption" style="text-align:center;color:#888;font-size:0.9rem;margin-top:0.3rem"></div>
<div id="net-card"></div>
:::

<script>
window.__viz = window.__viz || {};
window.__viz.network = function () {
  const net = window.__DATA_net;
  const W = 900, H = 620;
  const root = d3.select("#net-viz"); root.selectAll("*").remove();
  const nodes = net.nodes.map(d => ({...d}));
  const links = net.links.map(d => ({...d}));
  const color = d3.scaleSequential(d3.interpolateInferno).domain([0, Math.sqrt(net.prmax)]);
  const rscale = d3.scaleSqrt().domain([0, net.prmax]).range([2.5, 16]);
  const svg = root.append("svg").attr("viewBox",[0,0,W,H])
    .attr("style","width:100%;max-width:720px;height:auto;display:block;margin:0 auto;font:10px system-ui;cursor:grab");
  const tip = root.append("div").attr("style",
    "position:absolute;pointer-events:none;background:#222;color:#fff;padding:4px 8px;border-radius:4px;font:11px system-ui;opacity:0;z-index:10");

  const sim = d3.forceSimulation(nodes)
    .force("link", d3.forceLink(links).distance(34).strength(0.35))
    .force("charge", d3.forceManyBody().strength(-45))
    .force("center", d3.forceCenter(W/2, H/2))
    .force("collide", d3.forceCollide().radius(d=>rscale(d.pr)+1.5));

  const link = svg.append("g").attr("stroke","#999").attr("stroke-opacity",0.25)
    .selectAll("line").data(links).join("line");
  const node = svg.append("g").attr("stroke","#fff").attr("stroke-width",0.5)
    .selectAll("circle").data(nodes).join("circle")
    .attr("r",d=>rscale(d.pr)).attr("fill",d=>color(Math.sqrt(d.pr)))
    .style("cursor","pointer")
    .on("mousemove",(e,d)=>tip.style("opacity",1)
        .style("left",(e.offsetX+12)+"px").style("top",(e.offsetY-10)+"px")
        .html(`<b>${d.name}</b><br>${d.dependents} direct dependents`))
    .on("mouseleave",()=>tip.style("opacity",0))
    .on("click",(e,d)=>{ e.stopPropagation(); focusNode(d); });

  const labelG = svg.append("g").attr("pointer-events","none");

  node.call(d3.drag()
    .on("start",(e,d)=>{if(!e.active)sim.alphaTarget(0.3).restart();d.fx=d.x;d.fy=d.y;})
    .on("drag",(e,d)=>{d.fx=e.x;d.fy=e.y;})
    .on("end",(e,d)=>{if(!e.active)sim.alphaTarget(0);d.fx=null;d.fy=null;}));

  sim.on("tick",()=>{
    link.attr("x1",d=>d.source.x).attr("y1",d=>d.source.y)
        .attr("x2",d=>d.target.x).attr("y2",d=>d.target.y);
    node.attr("cx",d=>d.x).attr("cy",d=>d.y);
    labelG.selectAll("text").attr("x",d=>d.x+rscale(d.pr)+2).attr("y",d=>d.y+3);
  });
  // settle then freeze so it doesn't spin forever
  for (let i=0;i<320;i++) sim.tick();
  // crop the viewBox to the settled node cloud so there is no dead margin
  const rr = nodes.map(d=>rscale(d.pr)), pad = 12;
  const minX = Math.min(...nodes.map((d,i)=>d.x-rr[i])) - pad;
  const maxX = Math.max(...nodes.map((d,i)=>d.x+rr[i])) + pad;
  const minY = Math.min(...nodes.map((d,i)=>d.y-rr[i])) - pad;
  const maxY = Math.max(...nodes.map((d,i)=>d.y+rr[i])) + pad;
  svg.attr("viewBox",[minX, minY, maxX-minX, maxY-minY]);

  // ── Click a node to highlight its neighborhood (its direct connections) ──
  const nbr = new Map(nodes.map(n => [n, new Set()]));
  links.forEach(l => { nbr.get(l.source).add(l.target); nbr.get(l.target).add(l.source); });
  const baseCaption = `The core has <b>${net.nodes.length}</b> packages (k = ${net.k}). ` +
    `Click a node to highlight its neighborhood; click the background to reset.`;
  let focused = null;

  function reset() {
    focused = null;
    node.attr("fill-opacity",1).attr("stroke","#fff").attr("stroke-width",0.5);
    link.attr("stroke-opacity",0.25).attr("stroke","#999");
    labelG.selectAll("text").remove();
    document.getElementById("net-caption").innerHTML = baseCaption;
  }
  function focusNode(d) {
    if (focused === d) { reset(); return; }
    focused = d;
    const set = new Set(nbr.get(d)); set.add(d);
    node.attr("fill-opacity", n => set.has(n) ? 1 : 0.07)
        .attr("stroke", n => n === d ? "#111" : "#fff")
        .attr("stroke-width", n => n === d ? 2.5 : 0.5);
    link.attr("stroke-opacity", l => (l.source === d || l.target === d) ? 0.85 : 0.02)
        .attr("stroke", l => (l.source === d || l.target === d) ? "#444" : "#999");
    labelG.selectAll("text").data([...set], n => n.id).join("text")
      .attr("x", n => n.x + rscale(n.pr) + 1.5).attr("y", n => n.y + 2)
      .attr("font-size", n => n === d ? 7 : 5).attr("font-weight", n => n === d ? 700 : 400)
      .attr("fill", "#1a1a1a").attr("paint-order", "stroke").attr("stroke", "#fff").attr("stroke-width", 1.2)
      .text(n => n.name);
    const deg = nbr.get(d).size;
    document.getElementById("net-caption").innerHTML =
      `<b>${d.name}</b> — ${deg} direct connection${deg === 1 ? "" : "s"} in the core. ` +
      `Click it again or the background to reset.`;
    document.getElementById("net-card").innerHTML = window.packageCard(window.__pkgByName.get(d.name));
  }
  svg.on("click", reset);
  reset();
};
</script>

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal"}
Source: registry dependency graph, restricted to its k-core. Node color and
size encode PageRank. Label propagation on this subgraph does not resolve
distinct communities: the core is densely interconnected rather than partitioned
into separable clusters.
:::

# Package explorer {#explorer}

Per-package record for any of the `{julia} fmt_int(n_pkg)` packages:
dependencies, dependents, contributors, and **dependency-tree authors** — the
number of distinct commit-author accounts across the package together with its
full transitive dependency tree (that is, every account whose code is pulled in
when the package is installed).

```{julia}
#| output: asis
embed_json("pkgindex", IDX)
```

<div id="explorer">
  <input id="pkg-search" type="search" placeholder="Search packages by name…"
    style="width:100%;max-width:420px;padding:0.5rem 0.7rem;font-size:1rem;border:1px solid #ccc;border-radius:6px" autocomplete="off">
  <div id="pkg-results" style="margin:0.4rem 0"></div>
  <div id="pkg-card"></div>
</div>

<script>
window.__viz = window.__viz || {};
// Shared package-detail card — used by both the explorer and the network graph.
window.packageCard = function (rec) {
  if (!rec) return "<em>Package not found.</em>";
  const fmt = n => (n===null||n===undefined) ? "—" : n.toLocaleString();
  const jh = n => `<a href="https://juliahub.com/ui/Packages/General/${n}" target="_blank" style="text-decoration:none"><code>${n}</code></a>`;
  const gh = l => `<a href="https://github.com/${l}" target="_blank">${l}</a>`;
  const st = (label,val) => `<div style="min-width:110px"><div style="font-size:1.5rem;font-weight:700">${val}</div><div style="color:#888;font-size:0.82rem">${label}</div></div>`;
  const chips = arr => arr.length===0 ? '<span style="color:#999">none</span>'
    : arr.map(n=>`<span style="display:inline-block;margin:2px">${jh(n)}</span>`).join("");
  const contribs = rec.top_contributors.length===0 ? '<span style="color:#999">none recorded</span>'
    : "<ol style='margin:0.3rem 0 0 1.2rem'>" + rec.top_contributors.map(c=>`<li>${gh(c.login)} — ${c.commits.toLocaleString()} commits</li>`).join("") + "</ol>";
  return `<div style="border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:10px;padding:1.2rem 1.4rem;margin:0.6rem 0">
    <h3 style="margin:0 0 0.2rem">${jh(rec.name)} ${rec.isstdlib?'<span style="font-size:0.7rem;color:#888">(ships with Julia)</span>':''}</h3>
    <div style="color:#888;margin-bottom:0.8rem">v${rec.version??"—"} · ${rec.license??"license not detected"}</div>
    <div style="display:flex;gap:1.4rem;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:1rem">
      ${st("stars",fmt(rec.stars))}${st("direct dependents",fmt(rec.dependents))}${st("transitive dependents",fmt(rec.transitive))}${st("monthly requests",fmt(rec.requests))}${st("contributors",fmt(rec.contributors))}${st("dependency-tree authors",fmt(rec.trust))}</div>
    <details open><summary style="cursor:pointer;font-weight:600">Depends on (${rec.ndeps})</summary>
      <div style="margin:0.4rem 0">${chips(rec.deps)}${rec.ndeps>rec.deps.length?`<span style="color:#999"> +${rec.ndeps-rec.deps.length} more</span>`:''}</div></details>
    <details><summary style="cursor:pointer;font-weight:600">Depended on by</summary>
      <div style="margin:0.4rem 0">${chips(rec.dependents_list)}${rec.dependents>rec.dependents_list.length?`<span style="color:#999"> +${rec.dependents-rec.dependents_list.length} more</span>`:''}</div></details>
    <details><summary style="cursor:pointer;font-weight:600">Top contributors</summary>
      <div style="margin:0.4rem 0">${contribs}</div></details>
  </div>`;
};

window.__viz.explorer = function () {
  const idx = window.__DATA_pkgindex;
  window.__pkgByName = new Map(idx.map(d => [d.name, d]));
  const input = document.getElementById("pkg-search");
  const results = document.getElementById("pkg-results");
  const card = document.getElementById("pkg-card");
  const show = name => { card.innerHTML = window.packageCard(window.__pkgByName.get(name)); };
  input.addEventListener("input", () => {
    const qy = input.value.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (!qy) { results.innerHTML = ""; return; }
    const hits = idx.filter(d => d.name.toLowerCase().includes(qy))
      .sort((a,b)=>(b.dependents||0)-(a.dependents||0)).slice(0,12);
    results.innerHTML = hits.map(d =>
      `<button class="pkg-hit" data-name="${d.name}" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:420px;text-align:left;padding:0.35rem 0.6rem;margin:2px 0;border:1px solid #eee;border-radius:5px;background:var(--bs-body-bg,#fff);cursor:pointer">
        <b>${d.name}</b> <span style="color:#888;font-size:0.85rem">· ${(d.dependents||0).toLocaleString()} dependents · ${(d.trust||0).toLocaleString()} tree authors</span></button>`).join("");
    results.querySelectorAll(".pkg-hit").forEach(b =>
      b.addEventListener("click", () => show(b.dataset.name)));
  });
  // preload an interesting example
  show("Makie");
};
</script>

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal"}
Source: registry + GitHub, combined. "Monthly requests" is package-server
request volume (juliapkgstats.com) and includes CI traffic — read it as
install demand, not distinct users. "Dependency-tree authors" counts distinct
commit-author accounts across the package and its transitive dependency
closure; high-volume CI bots are filtered during collection.
:::

<!-- Boot all interactive figures once the DOM and vendored D3 are ready. -->
<script>
(function () {
  function boot() {
    if (!window.d3) { setTimeout(boot, 50); return; }
    try { window.__viz.scatter(); } catch(e){ console.error("scatter", e); }
    try { window.__viz.network(); } catch(e){ console.error("network", e); }
    try { window.__viz.explorer(); } catch(e){ console.error("explorer", e); }
  }
  if (document.readyState === "loading")
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", boot);
  else boot();
})();
</script>

# Methods & limitations {#methods}

The dataset is produced by a single reproducible pipeline and is contained in
one file. The following affect interpretation of the figures above:

- All figures reflect a single crawl on `{julia} SNAP_HUMAN`.
- **Repository-level vs package-level.** Stars, forks, issue counts, commit
  counts, and contributor lists describe *repositories*. Packages sharing a
  monorepo share these numbers; a subpackage can look more active or popular
  than its own code is.
- **"Requests" are not downloads or users.** Package-server request counts
  include continuous-integration traffic and mirror activity.
- **Commits are a weak proxy for contribution.** They omit review, triage,
  documentation, and design, and vary with squash-vs-merge habits. Named
  contributor rankings reflect commit reach, nothing finer.
- **Identity is a GitHub account.** Handle renames, shared/organizational
  accounts, and multiple accounts blur person-level counts. Bots are filtered
  by a best-effort list plus automated/AI accounts; some will slip through.
- **Dependency edges are latest-version hard dependencies between packages
  registered in General.** Weak/extension dependencies and historical
  dependency changes are not modeled. Standard-library coverage is partial:
  `{julia} n_stdlib_reg` of Julia's `{julia} n_stdlib` standard libraries are
  separately registered in General — the independently-versioned ones
  (`Statistics`, `TOML`, `Artifacts`, the `*_jll` binaries, …) — and so are
  graph nodes; the remaining `{julia} n_stdlib - n_stdlib_reg` (`LinearAlgebra`,
  `Random`, `Printf`, `Dates`, …) are not registry entries, so neither they nor
  dependencies on them appear. Because this coverage is partial, standard
  libraries are excluded from the ranked figures; counts for other packages are
  unaffected, since standard libraries are dependency sinks.
- **Coverage gaps.** Licenses were detected for ~66% of packages (GitHub
  reports none for the rest); GitHub metadata is missing for the few packages
  not hosted there.

The underlying dataset is a **knowledge graph** of
`{julia} fmt_int(Int(ntriples(DS)))` *triples*. A triple is the smallest unit
of the graph: a single fact written as *subject – predicate – object*, such as
*DataFrames → depends on → Tables* or *Flux → has contributor → CarloLucibello*.
Dependency edges, contributor links, star counts, licenses, download figures,
and every other attribute used above are each stored as one or more triples.
Together they describe `{julia} fmt_int(n_pkg)` packages as a single queryable
graph, and every figure on this page is computed from it directly.

This subject–predicate–object model is **RDF** (the Resource Description
Framework), a long-standing W3C standard for representing data as a graph.
Its defining feature here is that each package, person, and license is named by
a URL rather than an internal identifier — the package nodes are JuliaHub
pages, the people are GitHub profiles, the licenses are SPDX entries. Records
that share an identifier can therefore be joined across independently produced
datasets without a prearranged schema, which is the property usually meant by
"linked data." The full dataset is a single file and can be queried or combined
with other sources directly.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Now go ask your own questions.** The whole graph is in the
[SPARQL explorer](https://mthelm85.github.io/JuliaEcosystemGraph/explorer.html) —
pick an example query or write your own.
:::
